sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'Breakpoint contract' (2026-05-24, instance-debugger, artifact-only) + Net position 'Breakpoints' (2026-05-24, artifact) both describe pause-mode blocking as a post-acquisition runner-side wait, never a selection-time filter; doc=supervisor.md:31 pre-fix conflated selection-skips-paused with breakpoint dispatch-blocking in one sentence; code=lib/foundation/persistence/postgres/queue.go SelectCandidates SQL filters i.paused=false with no breakpoint/hit join; pause-mode blocking is runner-side waitForResume post-acquisition (lib/runtime/breakpoint_eval.go); test=conformance/select_candidates_paused.go covers the paused filter only, no selection-time breakpoint test exists.
note: The doc's single garbled sentence mixed a selection-time filter (paused instances) with a post-acquisition runner-blocking mechanism (pause-mode breakpoint hits), which the dossier's breakpoint contract describes as two distinct things. Rewrote supervisor.md:31 into two clear clauses so a reader isn't misled into looking for a selection-time hit filter that doesn't exist.

sources: dossier=no supervisor-dossier entry states 'decoupled tx' for the open verb; design corpus concept:fan-out ('Sub-claim atomicity per invariant 10: the rimsky-side acquisition transaction inserts the parent claim-handle row AND all sub-claim handle rows AND records all producer-returned addresses, or none of these') and concept:run-scope both state invariant 10 as acquisition-tx atomicity of inserts, not open-verb tx decoupling; doc=supervisor.md:27 (pre-fix) said the open verb 'runs in its own decoupled tx (invariant 10)', flatly contradicting :28's invariant 15 ('fires inside the rimsky-side acquisition transaction'); code=lib/runtime/runner_acquire_claims.go:84 calls s.Open inside the same tx as the later UpdateAddress:99, confirming invariant 15 and refuting the decoupled-tx gloss.
note: Line 27's gloss of invariant 10 was self-contradictory against line 28 and inconsistent with the canonical invariant-10 statement in concept:fan-out / concept:run-scope. Rewrote the gloss to match the canonical atomicity-of-inserts statement, removing the contradiction with invariant 15.

sources: dossier=Net position line 11 and Required behaviors line 35 assert 'attribute writebacks' bump last_progress_at (2026-06-17, b31002b8, transcript) but this is superseded by later, independently-corroborated design corpus: decision:uniform-attributes-delta ('there is no separate mid-dispatch attribute writeback... the mid-dispatch attribute writeback callback that an earlier asymmetric design forced is retired'), the explicitly-retired decisions/_retired/writeback-bumps-progress.md, decision:keepalive-endpoint, concept:attribute, and concept:signal, all of which agree attribute deltas arrive only on run-terminating verdicts and do not bump progress; doc=supervisor.md:11,19 (pre-fix) said 'attribute writeback' bumps the progress timestamp; code=only two BumpLastProgressAt call sites in lib/runtime exist -- keepalive.go (keepalive) and callback.go scratchStoreAdapter.Write (scratch, @story:opaque-executor-scratch) -- confirming no mid-dispatch attribute-writeback bump path exists.
note: The dossier's transcript-tier claim is itself stale: a later, multiply-corroborated decision (uniform-attributes-delta) retired the mid-dispatch attribute-writeback callback entirely, moving decisions/writeback-bumps-progress.md to _retired/. Current design and code agree the mid-dispatch progress-bump channel is scratch writeback, not attribute writeback. Fixed supervisor.md:11 and :19 accordingly. Note for the human: concept:node-run (not in this cluster) carries the identical stale phrase and was left untouched per scope.

sources: dossier=n/a (structural cross-concept consistency, not an intent claim); doc=concept:breakpoint Boundaries (rewritten by the breakpoint cluster) now states breakpoint owns 'breakpoint matcher evaluation and hit-recording at the pre-dispatch and post-terminal checkpoints' and explicitly assigns supervisor only 'the runner's checkpoint wiring -- invoking evaluation... -- and the blocked-runner resume-polling loop'; supervisor.md:19 (pre-fix) still claimed 'breakpoint checkpoint evaluation' verbatim in its own Owns line, conflicting with breakpoint.md's now-current Boundaries.
note: Verified against .ok-planner/design/concepts/breakpoint.md as it now stands: breakpoint owns matcher evaluation and hit-recording (the decision logic); supervisor owns only the checkpoint wiring (invocation) and blocked-runner polling (the mechanics). Narrowed supervisor.md:19's Owns line to match, replacing the 'breakpoint checkpoint evaluation' claim with wiring/polling language and a concept:breakpoint cross-reference.
